before: A unitless line-height is a multiplier. Descendants inherit the multiplier and apply it to their own font size. This helps a larger child keep proportional line spacing rather than inheriting one fixed pixel height.

The parent’s 20px font with 1.5 gives 30px line height. Its 30px child inherits 1.5 and uses 45px. If the parent instead specifies 30px, that fixed length is inherited, so the larger child also has 30px line height. Line height controls line boxes; it is not the visible ink height of every character.

Give the copy a 1.5 unitless line height so its 30px child uses 45px. The supplied HTML stays in index.html; edit the CSS. The checks inspect this small page, not every possible browser or accessibility requirement.
after: `line-height` sets the height used for a line of text. A value without a unit, such as `1.5`, is a multiplier. Multiply the text size by that number to find the line height.

Children can inherit this multiplier and apply it to their own text size. A fixed value such as `30px` is different: the child inherits that fixed length. Line height measures the line’s box, not the exact height of the ink in each letter.

Keep `line-height: 1.5` without `px`. If the child’s text size becomes 24 pixels, its line height becomes 24 × 1.5 = 36 pixels. Run the checks to confirm that the spacing follows the child’s text size.
